subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Interchangeable Parts: Whitney's Other Revolution
description: A 60-second lesson on Interchangeable Parts: Whitney's Other Revolution.

hook.text: Before 1800, every gun part was hand-fit. Break one and the gun was scrap.

buildup.text: Whitney proposed making parts to exact templates so any part fits any gun.

discovery.text: Standardized parts let unskilled workers assemble products quickly.

twist.text: Field repairs became trivial. Swap the broken part and keep fighting.

climax.text: This idea led to mass production and made modern manufacturing possible.

punchline.text: Make every part the same and repair becomes replacement.

quiz.question: What was the key advantage of interchangeable parts?
options: Parts cost more but lasted longer than hand-fitted ones
Any matching part fits any unit, enabling mass production and easy repair
Only highly skilled workers could make interchangeable parts
